title: Saudi Arabia Signs First Defense Pact With Damascus, Russia Deploys Its Rassvet Satellite Network Over Ukraine, and the US Space Force Faces a $1B Comms Gap
subhead: Riyadh has signed its first formal defense cooperation agreement with Syria's new leadership to rebuild the country's armed forces, marking a major realignment in Middle Eastern military partnerships. On the Ukrainian battlefield, Kyiv disclosed that Russia is now operating its own Starlink-style satellite network alongside cruise-missile-armed attack helicopters, while in Washington the Pentagon awarded Viasat up to $450 million for Golden Dome operations even as sources revealed a $1 billion satellite interoperability problem.

sections.heading: Riyadh Signs Defense Cooperation Agreement With Syria's New Leadership
sections.body:
Saudi Arabia has signed its first formal defense cooperation agreement with Syria's new leadership, establishing a bilateral military partnership after more than a decade of estrangement (Breaking Defense). Defense analysts told Breaking Defense that the accord will initially center on military training, intelligence sharing, equipment transfers, and advisory support to rebuild Syria's regular armed forces.

The agreement coincides with wider Arab efforts to curb non-state armed groups across the Levant and Mesopotamia. In neighboring Iraq, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi moved this week to target intermediary companies in defense procurement contracts and canceled contracts with three militia-linked firms operating at Mosul International Airport (Arab News, Star). Meanwhile, the US State Department approved a potential $100 million Foreign Military Sale to Jordan covering up to 1,500 APKWS II laser-guided rockets, MK-152 high-explosive warheads, and MK66 rocket motors (SavunmaSanayiST).
sections.whyItMatters: Saudi military training and equipment support for Damascus gives Syria's post-war leadership an Arab security partner, directly reducing the space previously occupied by Iranian and Russian military advisors.

sections.heading: Russia Fields Rassvet Satellite Comms and Helicopter-Launched Cruise Missiles
sections.body:
Ukrainian military intelligence disclosed on Friday that Russian forces are now actively using the new Rassvet low-Earth-orbit satellite network — Moscow's domestic counterpart to Starlink — for battlefield military communications over Ukraine (Defense News). The deployment gives Russian units higher-bandwidth command-and-control links that are harder for Ukrainian electronic warfare teams to jam than traditional tactical radios.

In parallel, newly released combat footage confirmed by the Russian Defense Ministry shows Mi-28NM attack helicopters firing jet-powered standoff cruise missiles — assessed by analysts as the S8000 Banderol or Dan-T — against targets in Ukraine (The War Zone, M5 Dergi). Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha also stated that Russian forces struck critical Ukrainian energy infrastructure using North Korean-supplied ballistic missiles ahead of winter (Euronews).

On the allied side, Spain is preparing a new 437 million euro military aid package for Ukraine following talks between Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and Zelensky in Madrid (M5 Dergi), while Britain and France will lead 2,800 troops from 11 nations in a two-week exercise in Poland testing logistics and force protection for a potential postwar deployment to rebuild Ukraine's military (Defense News).
sections.whyItMatters: Russia's fielding of sovereign LEO satellite communications and helicopter-fired standoff missiles narrows two tactical advantages Ukraine has relied on since 2022: Starlink connectivity and short-range air defense denial.

sections.heading: Pentagon Taps Viasat for Golden Dome as Space Force Hits a $1B Translation Problem
sections.body:
The US Department of Defense awarded Viasat an indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract worth up to $450 million to design, field, and scale the Mission Operation Center for the Space Data Network Backbone supporting the Golden Dome missile defense initiative (Breaking Defense).

However, industry and defense sources told Breaking Defense that key US Space Force satellites cannot currently communicate directly with one another across the SpaceX-built SDN Backbone and legacy Pentagon missile-tracking and communications constellations. Fixing the interoperability gap will likely require launching 12 to 13 dedicated 'Space Exchange Point' relay satellites at an estimated cost of roughly $1 billion (Breaking Defense).

In US air and ground procurement, operational US Air Force F-15EX Eagle II fighters have begun flying with conformal fuel tanks to extend range for Indo-Pacific missions, while the US Army unveiled its new clip-on MALET kit that converts standard mortar rounds into drone-dropped munitions (The War Zone). Meanwhile, Sierra Nevada Corporation formally exited the US Navy's T-45 jet trainer replacement competition, leaving a single bidder (The War Zone, Breaking Defense).
sections.whyItMatters: A $1 billion relay patch for satellites that cannot share data exposes the hidden cost of rapid, vendor-specific space procurement under the Golden Dome program.

sections.heading: European Hypersonic Interceptor Decision Nears and Baltic Navies Buy Finnish Mines
sections.body:
The European Commission is expected to select one of two competing industrial consortia by the end of November to develop a European interceptor capable of defeating hypersonic and ballistic missile threats, aiming for a system-level demonstrator by 2030 (Breaking Defense). In parallel, the UK and Italy completed the first successful internal weapons bay release test of the MBDA Meteor beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile from an F-35B Lightning II fighter (M5 Dergi).

In the Baltic Sea, Denmark and Lithuania became the latest NATO navies to sign contracts for Finland's 'Blocker' smart naval mines under a joint procurement scheme, strengthening maritime denial along Russia's Baltic approaches (Defense News). US European Command also launched a continent-wide counter-espionage and digital vigilance campaign for American personnel as hybrid sabotage threats mount across Europe (Defense News).
sections.whyItMatters: Baltic states are prioritizing immediate sea-denial weapons like smart naval mines that can be deployed today, while Brussels works on longer-term 2030 missile defense interceptors.

sections.heading: Kim Jong Un Inspects 10,000-Ton Warship as USS Theodore Roosevelt Reaches Singapore
sections.body:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspected the construction of a new large surface combatant at the Nampho Shipyard that naval analysts assess to be a 10,000-ton cruiser — roughly double the displacement of Pyongyang's 5,000-ton destroyers (USNI News). Meanwhile, satellite imagery analyzed by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) indicates China has made significant hull progress on its fourth aircraft carrier, the nuclear-powered Type 004, which could launch in 2027 (M5 Dergi).

For the United States, the USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) Carrier Strike Group — accompanied by cruiser USS Chosin and destroyers USS Paul Hamilton and USS Decatur — pulled into Singapore on Friday for its final port call before joining two other US carrier strike groups in the Middle East (USNI News, The War Zone). Elsewhere in the theater, the US Air Force outlined plans to revive WWII-era Pacific island airfields to support more than 6,000 aircraft operations annually, while the US Marine Corps stated it requires 40 amphibious warships — nine more than its current fleet of 31 — to meet global operational demands (Defense News, The War Zone).
sections.whyItMatters: Sending a third US carrier strike group to the Middle East pulls American naval tonnage west just as China and North Korea accelerate large surface ship construction in Northeast Asia.

bottomLine: Two shifts stood out in global defense today: Saudi Arabia's inaugural defense pact with Syria's new government begins reorienting Damascus away from its old military patrons, while Ukraine's disclosure of Russia's Rassvet satellite network shows Moscow closing part of the battlefield connectivity gap. In the West, procurement friction is visible on both sides of the Atlantic — from the US Space Force's $1 billion satellite translation hurdle and single-bidder Navy trainer contest to Europe's race to field hypersonic interceptors and Baltic naval mines before the end of the decade.
sources: Breaking Defense, Defense News, USNI News, The War Zone, SavunmaSanayiST, M5 Dergi, Euronews, Arab News, CSIS
